item.title: What we know as Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigns over affair allegations
item.description:
Jensen Huang resigned as CEO of Nvidia after he reportedly had two affairs, including one with a purported Chinese spy. Why it matters: It's impossible to overstate how critical Huang is to Nvidia, to the AI buildout, to the stock market and economy. His departure could, per Wall Street sources, be the catalyst that endangers a ballooning AI bubble. It's also unlikely to ease congressional scrutiny of the company or Huang himself. Driving the news: Nvidia's board named longtime CFO Colette Kress interim CEO, while launching a search for a permanent replacement. Kress, who joined Nvidia in 2013, will continue serving as CFO while overseeing the company. Harvey C. Jones was appointed Nvidia's first-ever board chair. item.title: Microsoft says services still returning amid widespread outage
item.description:
Microsoft was a source of frustration for computer users when it stopped working on Nov. 12, 2026. AP Photo/Michel Euler The Microsoft services outage that began on Nov. 12, 2026, is not like other internet outages. The failure affected the Microsoft 365 suite of productivity services, including the video conferencing and collaboration platform Teams, AI assistant Copilot and, significantly, the Outlook email service. Microsoft reported on Nov. 13 that the company is “continuing to see improvements in service availability” but that “some users may still experience intermittent access issues or delayed email delivery.” Despite decades of predictions about its decline , email remains a central pillar of how organizations function. Password resets, invoices, legal notices and cybersecurity incident response coordination all depend on it. The Microsoft 365 outage affected businesses,…

item.title: Why is Microsoft's outage lasting so long and will emails be lost?
item.description:
Microsoft suffered a global outage on Thursday and Friday. Hugh R Hastings/Getty Images Microsoft is suffering an outage of its core tools, disrupting millions of workers. How else do you cope, or celebrate, but by making memes? Some used clips from "Succession" to show the awkwardness, or joked about communicating with fire. Millions of workers have been unable to use their email and other core tools after a Microsoft outage . Microsoft first flagged the disruption midday Thursday, and problems continued into Friday. By 9 a.m., issues persisted, but the tech giant said it had "significantly reduced" the backlog of emails waiting to be delivered. It also said there was no evidence of malicious activity. item.title: UN chief says 'immediate and drastic' emissions cuts needed to avert climate change catastrophe
item.description:
Oceans and land have been absorbing a lot of the carbon emissions humans create. Dean Fikar/Moment via Getty Images Over the past two centuries, humans have pumped billions of tons of carbon dioxide into the atmosphere by burning fossil fuels , raising global temperatures in the process. Luckily for humanity, Earth has done what it could to soften the impact. The world’s oceans have absorbed 35% of carbon dioxide emissions from fossil fuels since 1990, our new research shows, and the forests and other plants of the world have absorbed another 13%. The oceans absorb a large amount of humanity’s carbon dioxide emissions from burning fossil fuels. That amount has been increasing, but new research suggests the increase will slow in the coming decades. item.title: Israel Used a U.S.-Made Missile to Kill Six at Gaza’s Nasser Hospital
item.description:
Throughout Israel’s war on Palestine, doctors Thaer Ahmad and Feroze Sidhwa spent months at Nasser Hospital in the southern Gaza city of Khan Younis, where they provided care as volunteers and survived a raid and an airstrike on the complex.
